name: Northern Peripheral Road (Delhi–Gurugram)

tolls.name: Bijwasan toll plaza
tolls.note: on the Delhi section; toll collection on the expressway began in November 2025

tollInfo.note: Tolled, and collected through FASTag. Indian toll rates are revised every year on 1 April.

timeline.event: 10 km Delhi section, including the airport tunnel, inaugurated (17 August), completing the expressway

history: The Dwarka Expressway, also called the Northern Peripheral Road, gives Delhi and Gurugram a second fast link besides the always-crowded NH 48. It was first planned in the mid-2000s as a Haryana road to open up new Gurugram sectors, but land disputes and court cases stalled it for years until NHAI took the project over and rebuilt it as a national highway. Because there was no room for a wide road on the ground, long stretches run high above the traffic on a single row of pillars, and near the Delhi end the road dives into a tunnel that connects towards Indira Gandhi International Airport. The Haryana part opened in March 2024 and the Delhi part in August 2025, and tolling began later that year.
facts: Long stretches run on a wide elevated carriageway carried on a single row of pillars.
The Delhi end includes an 8-lane shallow tunnel about 3.6 km long, with a branch tunnel to Terminal 3 of IGI Airport.
Passes Yashobhoomi, the big convention centre in Dwarka.
The 10 km Delhi section alone cost about ₹5,360 crore.
It is described as India's first eight-lane elevated urban expressway.
The road has four levels in places — an underpass, the ground road, the elevated carriageway and a flyover above it.
It was originally a Haryana state project and sat unfinished for years before NHAI took it over.
significance: Almost everything moving between Delhi and Gurugram used to squeeze onto one road, NH 48, and its Kherki Daula and Rajokri stretches were among the worst jams in India. The Dwarka Expressway gives that traffic a second route and, just as importantly, opens up dozens of new Gurugram sectors along its length, which is why so much housing and office building has followed it. It also gives west Delhi and Dwarka a direct road to Gurugram and to the airport that does not touch NH 48 at all.

travelNotes: End to end takes about 20–25 minutes when clear, against an hour or more on NH 48 in rush hour. Toll is collected by FASTag, and local commuters can buy a monthly pass. Two-wheelers and slow vehicles are not allowed on the elevated main carriageway, so use the service roads underneath, and be careful in the tunnel section where lane changes are restricted.
